[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Handling Hotfixes and Emergency Patches in Git"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When critical bugs are discovered in a production environment, a rapid response is crucial. Git provides effective strategies for managing hotfixes and emergency patches without disrupting the main development workflow. This tutorial outlines the recommended approach."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Hotfix Branch"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The first step is to create a dedicated branch for the hotfix. This branch should be based on the exact commit that is currently deployed in production. This ensures that the fix is applied to the correct version of the code."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"git checkout <production_tag_or_commit>
git checkout -b hotfix/<descriptive_name>"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace '<production_tag_or_commit>' with the tag or commit hash representing the deployed version. '<descriptive_name>' should clearly indicate the purpose of the hotfix (e.g., 'hotfix/security-vulnerability')."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing the Hotfix"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the hotfix branch is created, implement the necessary changes to resolve the issue. Follow standard coding practices, including writing tests to verify the fix and prevent regressions."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"# Make your changes
git add .
git commit -m "Fix: [Descriptive commit message detailing the hotfix]""},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Testing the Hotfix"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Thoroughly test the hotfix in a staging environment that mirrors the production environment as closely as possible. This includes functional testing, regression testing, and performance testing."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Merging the Hotfix"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"After successful testing, the hotfix needs to be merged into both the production branch (e.g., 'main' or 'master') and the development branch (e.g., 'develop')."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"git checkout main
git merge --no-ff hotfix/<descriptive_name>
git tag -a hotfix/<descriptive_name>-v1 -m "Tagging hotfix release"
git push origin main --tags

git checkout develop
git merge --no-ff hotfix/<descriptive_name>
git push origin develop"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"The '--no-ff' flag ensures that a merge commit is always created, preserving the history of the hotfix. Tagging the hotfix release allows for easy identification and rollback if necessary.  It is crucial to merge into 'develop' to ensure the fix is included in future releases."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Handling Conflicts"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Conflicts may arise during the merge process, especially if the development branch has diverged significantly from the production branch. Resolve these conflicts carefully, ensuring that the hotfix is correctly integrated without introducing new issues. Use 'git mergetool' to assist in conflict resolution."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"git mergetool"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Post-Deployment Verification"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"After deploying the hotfix to production, closely monitor the system to ensure that the issue is resolved and no new problems have been introduced. Implement monitoring and alerting to detect any anomalies."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Deleting the Hotfix Branch"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the hotfix has been successfully deployed and verified, the hotfix branch can be deleted."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"git branch -d hotfix/<descriptive_name>
git push origin --delete hotfix/<descriptive_name>"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Alternative: Cherry-Picking (Use with Caution)"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"In some specific scenarios, cherry-picking might be considered. However, it's generally discouraged for hotfixes because it can lead to inconsistencies in the commit history and make tracking changes more difficult. If you must use cherry-picking, ensure you understand the implications and document the process thoroughly."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"git checkout main
git cherry-pick <hotfix_commit_hash>
git push origin main"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"Note: After cherry-picking, you might need to manually resolve conflicts and ensure the changes are correctly applied."},{"order":28,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always base hotfix branches on the exact production commit."},{"order":30,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Thoroughly test hotfixes in a staging environment."},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Merge hotfixes into both the production and development branches."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use descriptive commit messages and tags for hotfixes."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor the system after deploying a hotfix."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid cherry-picking unless absolutely necessary and document the process."}]
